Hero Agencies and Sidekicks.text: Most professional heroes work through hero agencies. An agency is a licensed business led by a pro hero: it keeps an office, hires sidekicks and staff, covers a patrol area, answers emergency calls and handles press and merchandise. Agencies range from one-hero offices on a shopping street to towers with dozens of sidekicks, dispatch floors and private gyms. Sidekicks are licensed heroes employed by another hero's agency. Many are young pros gaining experience before opening their own offices; others stay for a whole career because they prefer teamwork to running a business. The lead hero answers for the agency's sidekicks in the field, and a famous lead hero's reputation carries the whole office. Pay comes from several sources. The government pays heroes for public service according to the cases they resolve and the help they give, so case credit matters: when several heroes work one incident, who made the capture or the rescue goes on record, and disputes over credit are common. Agencies also earn from merchandise, endorsements and appearance fees. Heroes team up for large incidents, either through operations planned with the police or by calling in allies from nearby agencies, and the hero leading the operation assigns the roles. Students meet agencies through internships and work-studies. Graduating Hero Course students apply to agencies the way other graduates apply for jobs, and the ambitious open their own offices once their reputations allow it.
